ambiguity.discussion:
Ambiguity: is the res_0p6 cytotoxic cluster 2 (439 cells; NKG7 in 99%) one population or NK cells plus CD8+ T cells? I reused the saved res_1 cluster 4 vs 6 contrast and did not recompute it.

Parameter sensitivity (computed): The cluster is single at res_0p3, res_0p6 and in the 70% downsample (308 cells, 286 from baseline cluster 2). It splits at res_1 (307 and 130 baseline cells) and res_1p5 (300 and 134). All 130 and 134 cells in the smaller piece come from baseline cluster 2. The split follows the resolution, and ARI against baseline falls to 0.66 at res_1. Resolution dependence alone does not show that two cell types exist.

Evidence for two populations (computed): res_1 cluster 6 has GNLY (97%), GZMB, FGFBP2, SPON2, PRF1, KLRD1, FCGR3A (89%) and TYROBP (94%). CD3D is detected in 7%, CD8A in 8% and CD4 in 0%. Cluster 4 has CD3D (84%), CD3E, CD8A (46%), CD8B, GZMK (58%), IL7R and CCL5. All of these are significant in the pairwise test, so cluster 6 is NK-like and cluster 4 is CD8 effector/memory-like (inference). NCAM1 is low in both (7% and 0.3%) and KLRF1 is only 27% in cluster 6, so the NK call rests on the cytotoxic program. The res_1p5 split gives the same pattern.

Shared program (computed): NKG7, CST7, GZMA, CTSW and HLA class I are high in both. PRF1 (52%), GZMB (34%), GNLY (35%) and FGFBP2 (33%) are also present in cluster 4. PMIDs 40538191 and 42682208 support NKG7/GNLY/GZMB as cytotoxic genes. They are not NK-versus-T discriminators. The shared program could reflect a common effector state, not a single lineage.

QC and size (computed): The medians are similar for cluster 4 and 6: 1975 vs 1892 counts, 804 vs 892 genes and 2.3% vs 2.0% mitochondrial reads. A library-size or mitochondrial artifact is therefore unlikely to explain the split. I did not test doublets. Myeloid-gene detection in cluster 6 coincides with NK-expressed TYROBP/FCER1G, so I read it as NK biology and not as doublet contamination (inference).

Unknown: Some CD3-negative NK cells may remain inside cluster 4, because CD3D dropout cannot be separated from true absence. The CD8 effector and NK programs may overlap in part. A continuum is not tested here. Resolving this needs protein data (CD3, CD56, CD16) or TCR information, which this pipeline does not provide. Markers were found in the same cells that were clustered, so p-values are exploratory.
